text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions: use clear, descriptive names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another good practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because other developers can find and fix problems quickly. In the long run, spending a little extra time writing clean code saves a lot of time and effort.
